title: How to Fail at AI Strategy: Hamel Husain & Greg Ceccarelli
talk_summary: A satirical 'invert always invert' talk listing anti-patterns of AI strategy: siloed teams, vague jargon-driven goals, tool-hammering instead of process analysis, off-the-shelf metrics, and refusing to look at data. The actionable content is the inversion: build evals tied to real failure modes, look at actual data/traces, involve domain experts, and fix processes before buying tools.

takeaways.technique: Custom evals tied to real failure modes, not off-the-shelf metrics
takeaways.what_they_do: They mock adopting every generic eval metric (cosine similarity, BLEU, ROUGE) and dashboards of numbers that don't track outcomes; the inversion is to define evals that measure your actual failure modes and cross-check with users/domain experts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: never ask whether they actually measure success ... optimize for cosign similarity BL and Rouge ignoring actual user experience

takeaways.technique: Look at the data / traces directly
takeaways.what_they_do: They satirize leaders who never inspect outputs and 'trust the AI's output without ever looking at it'; the inversion is routinely reading actual agent outputs and failure cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can absolutely 100% % trust the ai's output without ever looking at it yourself

takeaways.what_they_do: They mock 'whack-a-mole' tool adoption — new vector DB, new agent framework, fine-tune without measurement — instead of diagnosing the underlying process problem.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if they're not working just pick a new framework and vendor F tune without any measurement or evaluation

takeaways.technique: Clear, concrete goals instead of vague jargon
takeaways.what_they_do: They satirize ambiguous 'become the global AI leader in everything' policies and jargon that hides the jobs-to-be-done; the inversion is a clear business-on-a-page with defined scope.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your guiding policy should be both incredibly ambiguous and vague

takeaways.technique: Domain experts write/own prompts and context
takeaways.what_they_do: They mock letting only engineers write prompts and hiding work behind jargon (RAG, prompt injection) so domain experts can't participate; the inversion is keeping domain experts in the loop on prompts and context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: encourage Engineers not the people who might best understand your customers to write prompts
